samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Barkman takes Andrea's mermaid-necklace question ('I don't think those rules apply any more') as a test of natural law: self-evident principles — general beneficence (Glenn's 'shit creek' rescue, Morgan's warning that it 'takes away a piece of your soul'), special beneficence toward family (Lori's 'Don't be so trusting,' Morales's 'best for my family'), and piety (Guillermo staying with the abandoned elders) — still bind after the state's collapse, while 'do not steal' is merely derived, so the unowned necklace is fair game and Rick could take some but not most of Andrea's food. Aristotle's practical wisdom resolves the cannibal hunters' collision between preserving their lives and not killing innocents — starving is the morally preferable choice — since virtue weighs principles 'all things considered.' Against Carol's 'we can make new rules' relativism the natural law outlives governments, and Father Gabriel errs by calling walkers 'abominations,' conflating bad (dysfunctional) with evil (willful) — whereas the Governor, who knowingly ignores the moral law, reduces himself to walker level.

He deploys Hobbes's state of nature versus state of laws (Reds live in a state of war against Mars while Golds legislate in a state of law), Locke's suggestion that a sovereign can leave some people in the state of nature, Aquinas-style higher law, and H.L.A. samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The chapter maps four schools of ethics onto Fallout 4's Commonwealth: Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Preston Garvey's settlement defense as the mean between recklessness and cowardice and temperance as moderate chem use; Kant's Categorical Imperative is tested on stealing ammo in Concord and on the Battle of Bunker Hill choice to warn the Railroad, where loyal silence to Father fails universalization and treats synths merely as means. Aquinas's natural law ethics, keyed to the telos of power armor, workbenches, and Pip-Boys, condemns the Institute's creation of synths by analogy to the IVF debate while still demanding dignity for synths who already exist. samples.book: 154 - Doctor Strange and Philosophy - The Other Book of Forbidden Knowledge
samples.title: I Control It by Surrendering Control
samples.relation: Pérez stages the film's natural-law debate through Ayn Rand's Objectivism (Steve Ditko's avowed influence): Mordo's absolutism — 'there is no other way,' 'the bill comes due' — mirrors the axioms of existence, consciousness, and identity (A is A), with Cicero and Aquinas' divinely eternal natural law as the older backdrop. Rand's system is strained by the film's events: Wong dies and is un-died when Strange rolls back time in Hong Kong, and the Eye of Agamotto's time loop creates three simultaneous realities, so 'A' is no longer self-evidently one thing. The chapter concludes that Strange, exercising exactly the Objectivist freedom to think and choose, violates natural law in order to uphold it — sacrificing himself Prometheus- or Sisyphus-like in the Dormammu bargain — while Mordo's departure is wounded pride rather than principle.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 13. Carol’s Transformation
samples.relation: Delfino and Lesinski trace Carol's arc from abused wife (Ed's beatings, Sophia's death, "I didn't think I could be strong") to the judge-jury-executioner she once refused to be, reading the transformation through Aristotle's claim in the Nicomachean Ethics that repeated actions forge moral character. They then evaluate her killings: the murder of Karen and David fails on both act- and rule-utilitarian grounds (it did not stop the flu, and Glenn and Sasha survived while the group was shattered), whereas killing the delusional Lizzie is defensible both utilitarianly and by Aquinas's natural-law exception that an evildoer may be killed for the welfare of the whole community when no public authority remains. Her confession to Tyreese and Tyreese's forgiveness complete the phoenix rebirth symbolized by the burning walkers in "Consumed."

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Puts Aquinas's Murder Principle—the private, intentional killing of an innocent is always murder—to the Men of Mayhem, arguing the Sons lack the public authority Aquinas requires to kill even the guilty. The show itself erodes the state/private line Aquinas needs: corrupt agents Kohn and Stahl, and the CIA's Romeo Parada running the Galindo Cartel, make the badge look like no moral credential at all. The Doctrine of Double Effect sorts the rest: Jax shooting first in self-defense, Tara's morphine for the dying Unser, and Juice's hypothetical land-mine sacrifice are merely foreseen deaths, while Jax syringing Clay or Juice's intentional hanging would be murder. The chapter concludes that even if Aquinas condemns the Sons, his questions about authority, innocence, and intention are exactly the ones the show forces on viewers.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cooper argues The Wire stages two rival pictures of power: Hobbes's New School, where power is 'present means to some future apparent good', the good is only the apparently good relative to each desire, and honor is reputation indifferent to whether it is earned through love or fear (Clay Davis's graft, Ziggy's leather jacket, Avon displaying Brandon's mutilated body to 'send a message', Marlo spending exorbitant sums and torturing Butchie so his name keeps ringing out), and the Old School of Aristotle and Aquinas, where power is oriented to perfection and objective goods like family, friendship, and truth. Against the fear-based honor of the kingpins he sets McNulty's failed redemption and the successful reforms of Cutty's boxing gym, Walon's sobriety, and Bubs, whose prudence in taking the Sun job, temperance, justice at the Viva House, and fortitude in facing Sherrod's death embody the cardinal virtues, showing that even in the 'dark corner of the American experiment' virtue has the power to move.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Anti‐love Shows What Love Is
samples.relation: The chapter takes Irma Thomas's 'Anyone Who Knows What Love Is (Will Understand)?' - the song Brooker plants across five episodes - as the key to the series, defining love with Aquinas (to love is to wish the good by which the beloved flourishes, rooted in proper self-love, on an Aristotelian base) and evil as the void left where that good is withheld. Each episode that plays the song features characters who mishear it: Hot Shot's judges take Abi's sacrificial love song as an audition for submission to WraithBabes, Joe misreads Beth's song as meant for him and kills Beth's father in the resulting void, and Mia in Crocodile refuses the self-sacrificing loving act of confessing, murdering to fill the gap. Callow's pig-for-a-princess self-sacrifice, Theo's speech about commitment, and digital Walton dying to protect a copy of his son Tommy are the exceptions that know what love is, so the chapter concludes Black Mirror is as much about a world emptied of love as about dangerous technology.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Sin, Play, and the “Synagogues of Satan”
samples.relation: Rachael Sotos argues the Report performs Platonic play: like the divine puppet of Plato's Laws with its competing cords, Colbert reveals what moves us (fear, hope, the ThreatDown bears, the 'golden cord' of the good) and so teaches freedom through play. Colbert's pompous self-authority - claiming to be 'the canon and measure' of virtue in I Am America - parodies Aristotle's serious man (spoudaios, megalopsychos) and the sophists Protagoras and Prodicus with their Orpheus voices, proving Heraclitus right that 'time is a child at play' and Aristotle wrong that play is mere medicinal rest. Tracking the war on fun from Chrysostom through Aquinas's eutrapelia (there is sin in a lack of play) to Erasmus's Praise of Folly and the Puritans' ban on theaters as 'Synagogues of Satan,' she reads Colbert's playing-at-sin - the man-seed eugenics bit, the 'black friend' boasts, the Ellen DeGeneres Paradox on Wikiality - as Erasmian folly that heals America's Puritan hangover in the culture wars.

samples.title: a8.xhtml
samples.relation: Garcia argues Tolkien writes with a virtue-ethical moral theory: Middle-earth peoples are characterized by moral traits (noble eagles, cruel orcs), intentions matter (Bilbo is not to blame for the discomforting barrel escape because he meant rescue, and he turns back through the mountain tunnels because loyalty and courage demand it), and the book's drama is the tension between Aristotle's 'great-souled' proper pride and Aquinas' Christian humility. Thorin's pride (self-styled 'King under the Mountain', refusing Bard's just claim), Smaug's vanity that Bilbo flatters to find the bare patch, and the dragon-sickness illustrate pride as vice, while Bilbo's growth - believing after the spiders that 'there was more in him' yet accepting Gandalf's 'you are only quite a little fellow in a wide world' with a laugh - exemplifies correct self-assessment between vanity and undue humility.

samples.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
samples.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
samples.relation: Spencer gives a phenomenological account of bodily transformation in the films: with Merleau-Ponty, Peter's new body changes his world — walls become surfaces to climb — and grants motor knowledge that needs no calculation, while Norman Osborn's deliberately seized powers feed pride and Doc Ock's grief shows how transformation can sweep a weak will into vice. Virtue, on Aquinas's definition as the perfection of a power, develops only through choices and habits worked out across a whole life, so ethics is deeper than rule-following. With Levinas, the call to goodness is experienced bodily: sympathy with others' suffering draws Peter out of himself — he rushes into a burning building even when powerless in Spider-Man 2 — and the Green Goblin lives a self-contradiction by feigning deafness to it, while eros for Mary Jane both distracts from and ennobles the quest.

samples.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
samples.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bill Davis argues that Narnia works as a classical moral-education environment: against Experiment House's science-worship, Narnia supplies the three ingredients Aristotle and Aquinas require, namely instruction, virtuous exemplars to imitate (Reepicheep's courage, Puddleglum's temperance), and habituation through repeated right action, which together transform Peter's indecision, Edmund's treachery, Lucy's envy, and Jill's timidity. What finally lasts beyond Narnia, he contends, is a transforming encounter with Aslan: Eustace's dragon skin torn off by the Lion, Jill's drink at the stream where 'there is no other stream,' and Digory's tearful confession. He closes by arguing today's self-esteem-based character education cannot replicate this, since it pursues virtue from love of self rather than love of the good.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: Redemption
samples.relation: Stephen Bilynskyj tests John Hick's soul-making theodicy—that God allows suffering because virtues like courage, temperance, and compassion need pain to form—against Cash's life and songs. Using Aristotle on habituation by pleasure and pain (Cash's first amphetamine euphoria and the ostrich-attack painkillers as missed occasions for temperance) and Aquinas on innate aptitude and divinely infused virtue, he argues virtue can form without suffering (by genes or miracle), so soul-making alone cannot justify evil, as Cash himself implies about his mother's grief after Jack's death. Cash instead locates redemption in Christ's suffering ('Redemption,' 'Why Me, Lord?'), while the intervention by his son John Carter shows pain still occasioning real growth in temperance.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jessica Miller shows Katniss coded masculine, since Collins built her from Theseus and Spartacus and her breadwinning, hunting, and defiance fit masculine norms, while Prim embodies everything Beauvoir says civilization 'produces' as feminine, and Panem itself proves oddly gender-neutral: women work the mines, Finnick is the sex symbol sold by Snow, and Coin is as ruthless as any man. She then reads Katniss's romance performance through Judith Butler: the kisses, caresses, and televised wedding gowns do not express a preexisting femininity but constitute one, down to Butler's radical claim that sex itself is a cultural norm, which reframes even the Games' reaping of one boy and one girl as a gendered ritual rather than a presocial biological fact. Cinna's burning bridal gown that transforms Katniss into the mockingjay makes the political payoff explicit: gender performed strategically becomes the rebellion's power, and the hunter-and-baker partnership offers an alternative to the dominant romance script.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Mirror, Mirror
samples.relation: Sailors convicts Dorothy of being the stereotypical female of Baum's and Fleming's versions, disowning responsibility for killing both witches and living to please others, then contrasts her with Elphaba of Wicked as a feminist hero who leaves home, protects Animals, and mixes 'hot' male and 'cold' female anger into a single fury. She reads Elphaba's indeterminate gender through Marilyn Frye's point that easily identifiable groups are the easiest to oppress, through de Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but becomes a woman' and Mill's line that the 'nature of women' is an eminently artificial thing. Singer's liberation logic, together with the Wollstonecraft-Taylor 'Vindication of the Rights of Brutes' episode and the ecofeminist link between the oppression of women and animals, is applied to Elphaba's Animal-rights activism and her position as 'neither man nor beast,' before the Witch's mirror recognition of Dorothy forces the author to soften her verdict.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 9. Another Wig Underneath
samples.relation: Cooper argues that the 'vulnerability' Drag Race demands is really a marketable persona, not truth. Working through Butler's Gender Trouble (built on Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes a woman'), she concedes drag reveals gender's imitative structure, but shows it also confirms identity: Latrice Royale's padded 'Natural Woman' lip sync reads as authentic, and trans queens like Peppermint and Gia Gunn use drag to articulate womanhood, with Husserl's intersubjectivity invoked to insist that constructed gender is no less real for not being empirical. Willam's edit-spliced 'I'm not acting' breakdown and Shannel's deliberate wig-doff show honesty becoming inconsequential next to spectacle, while Untucked's Interior Illusions Lounge is framed as Sartre's No Exit hell of unending observation. Against RuPaul's 'born naked' self-help nihilism ('identity is a joke'), she ends warning that the show no longer lets Katya take off the chicken suit.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Gutwald takes seven-year-old Charlotte Benjamin's viral letter ('all the girls did was sit at home, go to the beach, and shop... but the boys went on adventures, worked, saved people') to argue the LEGO Friends theme is Wollstonecraftian 'friendly sexism' — revering girls as pretty play-things in a house-bound Heartlake City rather than oppressing them outright. Following Beauvoir's 'One is not born, but rather becomes a woman' and her point that men describe the world from their own perspective, plus Mill's Subjection of Women observation that argument alone cannot beat a 'mass of feeling', she explains how pinkified toy segregation feeds implicit bias, schemas, and stereotype threat in both girls and boys. Her fix is structural: make Friends bricks and mini-dolls compatible with the rest of the system ('Let the Friends go to Space!') and return to the gender-neutral 1981 'What it is is beautiful' ad.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 14. Re Production
samples.relation: Framed as leaked Project memoranda, the chapter argues Projects Leda and Castor embody philosophy's male-rational/female-reproductive dichotomy: Aristotle's function argument defined the human good (eudaimonia) through rationality while relegating women to reproduction, and the clones' engineered diseases literalize the split — fatal illness of the reproductive organs in the Leda clones, of the brain in the Castor. Simone de Beauvoir's Second Sex supplies the critique: "woman" treated as synonymous with womb, the Other denied the rich self-definition granted men, visible in Leda's passive unmonitored clones versus Castor's self-aware, active brothers. Combining a redeemed Aristotle (practical wisdom shows virtuous potential is not set by biological sex) with Beauvoir's free, independent woman, the chapter concludes both reproductive and rational autonomy must be restored to the clones of both sexes.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 13. How to Be a Dwarf
samples.relation: Using Carrot (a human raised in a dwarf mine who is accepted as a dwarf), Cheery Littlebottom (an openly female dwarf), and Gladys the golem, the chapter argues that social identity is neither biology nor a one-time choice but an ongoing performance that must also be recognized by insiders and outsiders. It applies de Beauvoir's 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' to Cheery's creation of a female dwarf gender against the deep-downers' equality that treats every dwarf as male, and reads the black ribboners versus the Magpyrs as assimilation versus doubling down on identity. Essentialist outsiders like Fred Colon and the Campaign for Equal Heights fail because they cling to stereotypes when individuals like Cheery or Carrot do not fit the mold, while Vetinari's indifference and Mrs. Cake's accommodations leave identity to those who must choose and perform it.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Sansa's journey from tourney-romance believer to 'they are no true knights' anchors a feminist argument that chivalry is unjust as a code, not merely corrupted by bad knights like Ser Gregor and Ser Meryn Trant, who beats Sansa at Joffrey's command. The pedestal, as Gloria Steinem says, is a prison: chivalry makes knights eternal guardians and ladies permanent childlike wards, a move the chapter explains through Spivak's account of saviors who turn the people they help into dependents and through Beauvoir's point that the custom of ladyhood manufactures the very 'fact' of female fragility it claims to protect. Arya's needlework, Brienne's unbeaten sword, Loras crowning Sansa while loving Renly, and Varys's riddle on power show the knight/lady roles are neither natural nor exhaustive, so 'there are no true knights' because chivalry itself blocks human flourishing.

samples.book: 179 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - Link Outside the Box
samples.title: Zelda and Reality
samples.relation: Joyce Havstad and Iris Jahng catalogue the women of Zelda — Zelda's many incarnations, Impa, the Twinrova sisters, the oracles Din and Nayru, Midna — finding the typologies of maiden, mother, and crone, then explain them with Beauvoir's The Second Sex: the myth of woman (Mother, Wife, Idea), femininity as made rather than born, and woman's enforced passivity against man's transcendence. Zelda is woman as Idea, traced to Platonic Forms: young, beautiful, virtuous, and radically passive (turned to stone in The Minish Cap, asleep through The Adventure of Link, imprisoned in nearly every game), an object that exists to motivate Link's heroism. Significantly, only the masculine-garbed Sheik and the pirate Tetra escape passivity, a shift the authors link to Miyamoto's design philosophy of 'reality over realism' and to changing conceptions of women.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rollin opposes mandatory helmet laws by contrasting two conceptions of freedom: the Hobbesian absence-of-constraint view ('go to hell in my own way', from Pinocchio's 'no strings on me' to the trapped coyote) and the rational-order view running from Plato (ranked classes, noble lies, censorship, contempt for democracy) through Rousseau's 'forced to be free', which Popper already identified as the enemy of the open society. Since, as the obesity-as-disease example and Robert Paul Wolff's expert-government argument show, we cannot claim certainty about value judgments the way we can about fractures, paternalism fails: if danger justified coercion we would have to ban motorcycles, skiing, parachuting, and bull-riding alike. Helmet laws in effect claim society knows what you ought to want better than you do, and Rollin's answer to his British colleague's 'what will you do if you injure your brain?' is to join the Department of Food Science and Nutrition.

samples.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
samples.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
samples.relation: Goguen reads the Winchesters through two masculine ideals: the warrior (Dean and Michael, chivalric protection culminating in Dean's 'protecting Sam... it's who I am') and the sovereign (Sam and Lucifer, whose freedom is analyzed with Isaiah Berlin's negative and positive liberty, with nods to Hobbes's absolute sovereign and Nietzsche's Übermensch). The show's stoic culture, where 'baring my soul like a freaking girl' is an insult, keeps the L-word unspoken, making Ellen's dying 'I will always love you, baby' to Jo a foil the brothers cannot match. Plato's Symposium, via Aristophanes' myth of split soulmates, and Aristotle's claim that the purest love is between virtuous male friends make sense of the 'psychotically, irrationally, erotically codependent' bond, and the chapter concludes that true masculinity requires embracing the seemingly supernatural: love.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 4. Non-State Enemies of Freedom
samples.relation: Nash argues 1984 has been misread as a critique of state power alone; through Newspeak's silencing of thought (in the tradition Austin, MacKinnon, and Langton developed) it shows how any concentration of power oppresses via control of words, data, and information. Drawing on Goldstein's manual's debt to James Burnham's managerial revolution and Sheldon Wolin's 'inverted totalitarianism', she reads the non-centralized Oceania as a warning about non-state enemies: corporations, think tanks running the 'Tobacco Strategy', and global institutions peddling misleading poverty statistics. Popper, Arendt, and Berlin exemplify the state-focused liberalism she thinks blinded us to these horizontal threats, while the Newspeak appendix's past tense shows Orwell expected totalitarianism to be beatable through evidence and democracy.

samples.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
samples.title: 24. A Modern utopia
samples.relation: Robin Bunce reads 2049 as a libertarian utopia realized: a Los Angeles without welfare, planning, or federal power, where Hayek's market knowledge and Nozick's minimal state have won and everything from water to children to replicants is voluntarily bought and sold. Yet the result is a slave state, and Nozick's freedom-as-non-coercion — the negative liberty Berlin also held — cannot explain Luv, the film's most privileged character, who is nonetheless a slave because her existence hangs wholly on Wallace's will. Quentin Skinner's and Algernon Sidney's neo-Roman liberty, independence from another's will, explains her fear, and the Baseline, like Orwell's 'Thou Art', reveals an ambition to enslave not actions but souls; Freysa's 'we are our own masters' is a republican declaration of independence.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lowe stages a 'Tolerance Bowl' between Sheldon's scientism and Mary's fundamentalism, opened with Berlin's liberal answer to pluralism — everyone entitled to their opinion, yet Sheldon insists 'evolution isn't an opinion, it's fact' and Mary's tolerance becomes its own tyranny. Davidson's argument that there is no very idea of a radically different conceptual scheme shows mother and son argue from shared concepts (DNA, intelligent design), but both remain metaphysical realists who cannot brook disagreement, while Rorty's 'the world does not speak' antirealism encourages fallibilist tolerance only to congeal into a 'what-we-have' dogma of its own that cannot account for genuine plurality. Nobody wins the bowl: each worldview makes tolerance hard in its own way.

samples.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
samples.title: 3. Click Bait for Black Fish
samples.relation: Porot reads Elliot through Berlin's positive liberty: people are enslaved to their lower selves - the 'daemons' of addiction and primal urge Elliot describes in 'eps1.3_da3m0ns.mp4' - and freedom requires a contract in which an external force holds you to your higher self. Elliot writes such contracts with Shayla over his drugs and imagines Mr. Robot as the paternalistic enforcer who pushes him off the pier when he breaks his word, while corporations run the reverse contract, 'hacking' people from within through addictive sugar, clickbait, and advertising. The black fish dream crystallizes this: everyone at the office devours the confined fish of reverse-contract slavery while Elliot alone eats Pop's pie - freedom through the father figure of Mr. Robot.

samples.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
samples.title: Synthesis
samples.relation: Elizabeth Brake asks what freedom Dylan's outlaw persona - refusing Maggie's Farm, possessive love, and conformity - actually wins, framing the answer with Berlin's two concepts of liberty. Dylan's negations look like Berlin's negative freedom, but Hegel's critique of the "freedom of the void" shows mere refusal ends in emptiness, so she reconstructs a Millian and Emersonian ideal of self-realization for which negative liberty is only the condition. "To live outside the law, you must be honest" supplies the synthesis: outside social law the free person answers to the Emersonian law of his own nature and to undistorted honesty with others, a more severe morality Dylan shares with Emerson and Nietzsche.

samples.book: 252 - Better Call Saul and Philosophy - I Think Therefore I Scam
samples.title: 23. Why Does Jimmy Get to Determine Chuck’s Healthcare
samples.relation: The chapter uses Chuck's EHS to probe when paternalistic intervention against a competent person's will is justified. It argues Chuck is epistemically irrational (the hidden battery and electrified bed disprove his causal beliefs) yet notes, via Sharon Street and Nietzsche, that we all act on 'illogical' but coherent evaluative attitudes, so absurdity alone cannot license Dr. Cruz's push to commit him. Invoking Isaiah Berlin's warning against oppression in the name of someone's 'real self' and Mill-style concern for self-regarding choices, it finally uses Simone de Beauvoir to distinguish Jimmy's genuine devotion to Chuck from Chuck's controlling 'tyranny,' which shaped Jimmy's turn into Saul.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: How to Misunderstand Politics Completely
samples.relation: Melançon argues Radiohead's real politics lie not in the overt content of Hail to the Thief but in a Camusian movement from absurdity to revolt: 'Exit Music'''s violent shift from Romeo's tender 'you' to the distorted 'we hope that you choke' enacts revolt against imposed rules and wisdom, while the android of 'Fitter Happier' ('a pig in a cage on antibiotics') and the wished-for alien of 'Subterranean Homesick Alien' dramatize absurd life under others' dictates. Following The Myth of Sisyphus and The Rebel — 'I revolt, therefore we are' — he shows how the songs' 'I' becomes a collective 'we' ('Karma Police', 'Lucky', 'Dollars and Cents') whose revolt, like Sisyphus's conscious walk back down the mountain, affirms life without ever justifying murder. Merleau-Ponty's philosophy of expression then explains why the songs are political anyway: artists express a still-unspoken 'fever' (it took years before 'Nude' could be said), creating a public and a common world — politics as unveiling rather than governing, down to 'Electioneering'''s admission that the band too campaigns for our vote.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Would You Help Me to Carry the Stone
samples.relation: Weinstein argues critics who call Waters a gloomy misanthrope misread him: he is an existentialist whose work maps point for point onto Camus's absurd, the human demand for unity endlessly frustrated. Waters's imagery tracks Camus's: the sun (Plato's cave symbol of the good, and the light Sisyphus loved on earth) against the eclipsed moon of death and madness; the stone we secrete through failed communication ('the bad blood slows and turns to stone' in 'Dogs,' 'would you help me to carry the stone' in The Wall) against Sisyphus's rock; and Pink's Trial, condemned for 'showing feelings of an almost human nature,' replaying Meursault's condemnation for failing to cry at his mother's funeral. Since the institutions of home, school, military, and the music industry's machine block every genuine encounter, Waters's persistence in making art that mostly fails to communicate is itself the absurd revolt, so with Camus one must imagine Sisyphus happy, and Weinstein imagines Waters happy too.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: The Horizon of Disenchantment Film Noir, Camus, and the Vicissitudes of Descent
samples.relation: Alan Woolfolk reads noir through Weber's disenchanted world and Charles Taylor's cultural horizons, arguing the noir protagonist can neither resist the darkness like Conrad's Marlow nor fully embrace it like Coppola's Willard, remaining trapped between times in an ethically irrational universe. He contrasts Camus, who counters disenchantment with an ethic of honesty grounded in a Rousseauian benign nature (The Stranger's Meursault) and with the Baudelairean dandy as aesthetic model, against noir protagonists (Neff, Marlowe, the Swede, Scottie Ferguson) whose 'banked fires' fail and who lose self-possession. Drawing on Freud's id as 'a cauldron full of seething excitations,' he argues the femme fatale drags the protagonist downward into the timeless unconscious where anything is possible (Noah Cross's incest in Chinatown, the radioactive box in Kiss Me Deadly, Body Heat's Ned Racine), and reads noir as backward- and downward-looking through Palmer/Bakhtin's chronotope.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rachel Robison-Greene applies Camus's absurdity to the series: walkers, like digger wasps, live meaningless loops without the self-reflective consciousness that 'poisons' experience, while survivors like Morgan longing for Jenny and Andrea for fishing trips with her father embody the clash between human longing and an indifferent universe, exactly as in Camus's The Plague at Oran. Suicide (Jacqui and Jenner as the CDC explodes) and religious consolation are escapist responses—the latter 'philosophical suicide'—so the authentic path is the absurd hero: Rick searching Atlanta for his family, Daryl fighting uphill with an arrow in his side, the Vatos group caring for abandoned elders. Weighing Nagel's objection that absurdity arises from our clashing subjective and objective perspectives, she concludes we cheer Rick shooting Sophia in the barn because subjective commitment stays noble even where objective meaning is nowhere to be found.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rachel Robison-Greene reads the survivors through Camus: walkers are mere digger wasps, living tedious, meaningless loops without the consciousness that would make it agonizing, but the living - Morgan longing for the real Jenny back, Andrea losing Amy - face the absurd confrontation between human longing and an indifferent universe, just like Oran in Camus's The Plague. Of Camus's options, suicide (Jacqui and Dr. Jenner staying in the exploding CDC) and religion ('GOD FORGIVE US' on the farmhouse wall) are escapist, so she offers the absurd hero: Sisyphus with his rock, Rieux with his plague, matched by Rick hunting Atlanta for his family, Merle's self-preservation, and Daryl fighting uphill with an arrow in his side. Against Nagel's ironic alternative, she argues we cheer Rick when he alone will shoot Sophia in Hershel's barn because his subjective commitments stay noble even with no objective meaning behind them.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 2. Maybe Jenner Was Right
samples.relation: Cowan uses Jenner's suicide in the exploding CDC (1.6 'TS-19') to pose Camus's question 'Why should I not commit suicide?', and rejects Jenner's despair the Camusian way: Michonne in 4.9 'After' - slaying her own walker look-alike and then her two pet walkers - is his Sisyphus in revolt, unlike Gareth, whose revolt lacks the respect for human dignity that makes Sisyphus happy. He then objects that Camus never explains why human life has intrinsic dignity in a godless universe, noting that Sartrean authenticity could equally license the Governor's Woodbury experiments or Gareth's cannibalism, and turns to Hershel's providential hope as the religious alternative. Following Plantinga, he argues belief in God can be properly basic through a sensus divinitatis - Hershel seeing God's hand in 2.4 'Cherokee Rose' and the tornado-spared barn of 5.10 'Them' - so if God exists, Jenner was not right.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Fagan traces the show's ubiquitous 'Game' to Heraclitus's fragment of Aion as a child moving game-pieces: the drug trade, police, docks, schools, and newsroom all have rules, fixed roles (D'Angelo's chess lecture where pawns get capped quick), winning reduced to stats, strife as justice, and cyclical recurrence with 'new dancers, new faces around the throne.' Bodie's dying rant that the game is rigged, the failed escapes of Wallace, D'Angelo, and Stringer's 'games beyond the game,' and even Omar's fatal loyalty to Butchie show that neither rule-following nor Omar-style code-breaking gets a piece off the board. Against critics who call the show nihilistic, he argues it rejects the Heraclitean picture through Camus's rebellion: Colvin, Bubbles, and Cutty fashion dignity by resisting the Game even though rebellion almost certainly fails.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Svolba and Flanders read Curb as an extended investigation of civility—the rules of what people 'just don't do,' from using the doctor's phone to touring Susie's new house to singing 'Happy Birthday' at Ben Stiller's party. Larry plays Socratic gadfly: refusing the tour harms no one and treats no one unfairly, and Susie's only justification ('it's just not done') is circular, so his incivility can seem admirable, even like minor civil disobedience. Against this, the chapter argues (crediting Cheshire Calhoun) that rules of civility are conventional vehicles for communicating respect for others' feelings and interests—what matters to Susie ought to matter to Larry—and, more consequentially, that a social world full of Larry Davids would be unbearable. Larry's own Golden-Rule litmus test, by which he never talks in movie theaters because he would hate it himself, misses this point, since civility is precisely about what others happen to want and like.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cherry asks why even law-abiding citizens in The Wire obey the no-snitching code, answering through Cornel West's diagnoses: the police's 'evangelical nihilism' is Thrasymachus's might-makes-right acted out by Herc, Carver, and Prez at the Towers and by Walker breaking Donut's fingers, while the bosses' 'paternalistic nihilism' (Burrell juiking stats for Royce) leaves citizens not merely frightened but healthily hopeless, as Randy's 'You gonna look out for me? You promise?' shows after Herc burns him and the detail vanishes. Drawing on Angela Davis's argument that the criminal justice system inherited slavery's master-slave dynamic through the Black Codes, vagrancy laws, and the drug war, she reframes silence as active rebellion: a Gandhian philosophy of non-co-operation ('Fuck the Police') that withdraws the state's claim to citizens' dependence because witnesses like William Gant and Nakeesha Lyles are left unprotected.

samples.book: 208 - X-Men and Philosophy - Astonishing Insight and Uncanny Argument in the Mutant X-Verse
samples.title: X-Men and Philosophy
samples.relation: This block finishes Davis's essay (Xavier's 'good nonsense' rules vs. Magneto/Dennett/Hobbes evolutionary morality) then runs several more. Robichaud's 'Professor X Wants You' weighs whether Storm should join the X-Men or Brotherhood using Nozick's experience machine (Rogue vs. 'Eugor') for well-being and Dworkin's civil-disobedience tiers for when violent resistance is permissible. Housel's 'X-Women' reads Jean Grey, Rachel Summers, Scarlet Witch, Storm, Mystique, Rogue, and Kitty through Sartre's 'existence precedes essence,' bad faith, Ortega's project, and Baudrillard. McWilliams uses Singer's speciesism and human-rights declarations to ask if mutants deserve moral consideration and whether torture/experimentation on them can be justified. Darowski reads Deadpool's fourth-wall breaks as postmodern metafiction raising Plato's-cave ontological questions.

samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
samples.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
samples.relation: Alloy uses the problem of political obligation to split the heroes: against Plato's Crito, where Socrates refuses escape because even bad laws bind, Bruce Wayne simply flees arrest in Bruce Wayne: Murderer?/Fugitive, treating law as a tool of his war. He tests consent theory through Superman's chosen handcuffs in Man of Steel and Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's 'mortal god' versus Locke's natural-rights standard, lets Hume's objection sink tacit consent (Red Son Superman cannot really emigrate, and Batman would never leave Gotham), rejects gratitude theory via the Kents' adoption of Kal-El, and dismantles Batman's 'I'm not wearing hockey pads' defense with Nozick's Batman-lottery — concluding Superman's law-conforming restraint protects the public from him becoming Luthor's 'alien overlord', while answerable-to-no-one Batman remains a force of chaos.

samples.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
samples.title: Anarchism and the Beats
samples.relation: Ed D'Angelo argues the Beats had a philosophy after all: a romantic bohemian anarchism that made poetry a means to a religious transformation of consciousness, with political change following consciousness rather than the reverse. He shows Ginsberg inverting Plato's rationalist hierarchy (grounding reason in imagination and the body) and reads Beat 'criminality' as a shamanic journey to the unconscious underworld, distinct from Mailer's macho 'White Negro' hipster. He traces their lineage through Greenwich Village bohemia, Proudhon/Bakunin/Kropotkin anarchism, and pacifist anarchists like Rexroth and Dellinger, arguing the Beats rejected Marxist materialism and class warfare, and that the movement was 'born' out of Rexroth's anarchist poetry circle at the 1955 Six Gallery reading of 'Howl.'

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: “That Community’s a Lot More Wholesome and Functional than, Just for Example, Neptune Is”
samples.relation: Paul Hammond asks whether Veronica's habitual lawbreaking — switching the evidence tapes in the 'Pilot,' stealing Duncan's medical file, tricking Principal Van Clemmons — can be morally justified. He constructs a social-contract defense: Neptune's corrupt, class- and race-skewed sheriff's department under Don Lamb has failed to deliver the protection and justice that purchase citizens' obedience, releasing Veronica from her end of the bargain. Testing that defense against the Laws' speech in Plato's Crito (lawbreaking destroys the city; staying in Athens constitutes consent) and Kant's requirement that genuine law be universal, he concludes that where Neptune's civil law diverges from the moral law, Veronica's crimes can rise to a civil disobedience that is sometimes 'really just.'

samples.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
samples.title: This Is Our World
samples.relation: Miguel Sicart reads the 'Gnome Tea Party' — dozens of nearly nude gnome warriors parading in Ironforge to protest Warrior-class nerfs until Blizzard banned their accounts — as non-violent protest in the tradition of Thoreau and Gandhi. Against Blizzard's models of players-as-consumers and players-as-troublemakers, which he traces to Huizinga's Homo Ludens, he argues that players are Homo poieticus: creative beings who make the values they play by and act on them. Using the 'Flourishing Ethics' framework built from Aristotle's virtue ethics and Wiener's information ethics, he concludes that WoW's architectures of control and account-banning are an unethical design that damages players' capacity to flourish — Azeroth is our world too.

samples.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
samples.title: So, What’s the Bottom Line
samples.relation: James Klagge, defining terms in Socratic fashion, distinguishes bootlegs like Great White Wonder from piracy and argues unreleased Dylan material (the New York Blood on the Tracks, "Blind Willie McTell," the 1966 Live concert) has genuine musical and historical value. He rejects the Sophist view that morality is just self-interest and the relativist "everybody's doing it" defense, then weighs the artist's Lockean property and privacy rights against fans' rights of access, noting legal-but-immoral and illegal-but-moral cases in the spirit of Martin Luther King's civil disobedience. His verdict: bootlegging is morally acceptable when royalties are fair, stolen tapes are not used, and mainly public performances circulate.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bárcenas answers studies suggesting The Daily Show breeds youth cynicism by recovering the original 'dog philosophy': Cynics like Diogenes of Sinope lived shamelessly (the bathtub, the lamp in broad daylight, 'stand out of my light' to Alexander the Great) to expose the corrupt conventions of Athens's fragile direct democracy, where demagogues like Alcibiades seduced the assembly into debacles such as the Sicilian expedition. He reads Stewart as their modern heir, with 'Mess O' Potamia' and 'Crises in Israfghyianonanaq' against war demagoguery and the Cramer interview against financial-media dereliction, whose humor aims at Aristotle's anagnorisis, a sudden recognition of things as they really are behind flattering appearances (doxa). Cynical unpopularity (adoxia) is worn as a badge of truth-telling, and parrhesia, frank speech, becomes democratic shock therapy that awakens citizens' judgment rather than breeding apathy.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Presents three ancient alternatives to SAMCRO's warrior ethic. Diogenes the Cynic, 'the earliest of all the fathers of anarchy,' matches J.T.'s Harley-commune ideal — reject greed, convention, and wage slavery like Tig punching the clock at Teller-Morrow — but the chapter argues pure anarchy regenerates hierarchy: with no authority, revenge becomes the only justice and 'a big guy like Clay' mugs 'a small guy like Chuckie.' Plato's Republic supplies the reformist pole — impartial justice for all citizens rather than loyalty circles, rulers picked from proven warriors for wisdom (Tara belongs healing, not scheming), family curbed where it breeds Gemma-style favoritism — yet proves too authoritarian, so Aristotle's function argument (reason as the human ergon), virtue, and the three kinds of friendship (SAMCRO's pleasure-friendships, Clay–Unser's usefulness) sketch a livable middle way with duties even to strangers.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Over an evening at the Iron Post biker bar, Auxier maps four habitues onto the Hellenistic schools: Cowboy, the Vietnam chopper pilot whose bar is a Garden of modest pleasures, loyalty, and withdrawal from power games, is an Epicurean; the laconic Bear, who doubts that even possessing knowledge would make us better off and suspends judgment, is a Pyrrhonian (unlike the coffee-house Carneadean); Happy Jack, the 'true nature's child' of 'Born to Be Wild' who defies convention and keeps nothing six months, is Diogenes's Cynic; and Gary, the Vietnam-damaged recovering alcoholic, is a damaged Stoic who has not reached apatheia. He concludes that bikers are postmodern pagans whose philosophy is enacted rather than propounded, a Biker Platonism that refuses the Christian-Platonic divorce of body and spirit and lives by honor, freedom, and a pagan fatalism that accepts the consequences of one's choices.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: A Newspaper Gone to the Dogs . . . Enlightened Dogs
samples.relation: Bayan traces 'cynic' to the Greek kynikos ('doglike') and the philosophy to Socrates' virtue, poverty, and integrity, through the proto-Cynic Antisthenes to Diogenes of Sinope—the man in the tub, the plucked chicken at Plato's Academy, 'you can step out of my sunlight'—arguing that Cynicism is fierce moral opposition to sham and hypocrisy, which is exactly why the powerful smear cynics. Distinguishing The Onion's cool, Swiftian irony from postmodern 'pseudocynicism,' he concludes the paper is genuinely Cynical: headlines like 'Black Guy Asks Nation for Change' (the Obama reveal), 'God Angrily Clarifies Don't Kill Rule,' and 'Dictator Slays Millions in Last-Minute Push to Be Time's Man of the Year' nuzzle the kind, bark at the greedy, and bite scoundrels, so Diogenes would have read The Onion with paternal fondness.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: That’s His Story and He’s Stickin’ to It
samples.relation: Aaron Pratt places Buffett's 'island escapism' in the lineage of the ancient 'graceful life' philosophies: like Diogenes the Cynic, Buffett flouts social convention (pirates over Civil War generals, the beach over the rat race, 'Be good and you will be lonesome'), and like Epicurus he preaches pleasure with prudence rather than mere indulgence. 'Cheeseburger in Paradise' becomes Epicurus's command to know what you want and go get it, while the hung-over confession of 'Margaritaville' — 'I know it's my own damn fault' — supplies the Epicurean proviso that overindulgence ruins the pleasure it promises. The chapter closes by arguing that counter-cultures like Parrotheadism carry built-in safety features: careers and families force Epicurean prudence, keeping escapism a periodic liberation rather than social collapse.

samples.book: 265 - Mark Twain and Philosophy
samples.title: Chapter 12 The American Diogenes
samples.relation: Johnson argues Twain is best understood not as a religious skeptic but as an 'American Diogenes'—a Cynic of Christianity-as-practiced. As Diogenes 'defaced the coinage' to remove counterfeit customs, Twain uses 'sacred profanity' (honest, even profane speech that exposes phony piety, e.g. the swearing butcher, Satanic narrators in 'The Mysterious Stranger' and 'Letters from the Earth') to strike four counterfeit coins: superstition/special providence, hypocrisy, artificial 'Moral Sense'/conscience, and heavenly rewards. On death Twain matches Diogenes and Epicurus (annihilation is nothing to fear), and his self-description as 'Member at Large for the Human Race' mirrors Diogenes the cosmopolitan; Diogenes carries a lantern to find a real human, Twain a mirror to show we are worse than we think.

samples.book: 278 - Fashion – Philosophy for Everyone - Thinking with Style
samples.title: FASHION - PHILOSOPHY FOR EVERYONE
samples.relation: Pierlott examines sweatshops in the garment industry through the lens of ancient Cynicism (Antisthenes, the Stoics' Zeno of Citium and his thieving slave), using the Cynic critique of fashion-driven consumption to strip legitimacy from the demand that feeds sweatshops. He rebuts the 'inevitability argument' (comparing it to excusing the Holocaust as inevitable) and the free-choice defense using Aristotle's category of 'mixed' action — sweated workers' consent is coerced by desperate alternatives — and argues, via Adam Smith on the undervaluing of labor, that giant retailers like Wal-Mart distort natural labor prices. He stresses that sweatshops overwhelmingly exploit young women, tying objectification of women as fashion consumers to their oppression as producers.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: The Male Vampire as Metrosexual . . . Sort Of
samples.relation: Joan Grassbaugh Forry argues the 'vampire aesthetic' both enforces and destabilizes constructed norms of beauty and gender, reading vampire representation through Foucault's made soldier (the body produced by discipline rather than nature) and the Bartky-Bordo feminist analysis of disciplinary beauty practices. Vampires are effortlessly, youthfully beautiful — exempt from the dieting, grooming, and ornamentation that produce femininity — yet their beauty must appear natural, which is exactly the demand beauty culture makes of women; Queen Akasha, Drusilla, and child-vampire Claudia are ultra-feminine femmes fatale whose threat is neutralized by childlike femininity and punished by death or ridicule (Claudia ashes in the sunlight, Drusilla is made to look foolish), while the feminized male protagonists — Louis and Armand in Interview with the Vampire, Angel and nail-polishing, Passions-watching Spike in Buffy, Langella's elegant Dracula — turn beauty, taste, and expressed emotion into audience identification and beautiful martyrdom. The payoff: in the realm of the Undead the male vampire becomes a beautiful martyr while the female vampire becomes a disastrous woman we love to hate.

samples.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
samples.title: The ageing woman as (American) horror story
samples.relation: The chapter theorises the 'abject barren body' — the menstruating, menopausal and post-menopausal woman — connecting menarche as an upswell of feminine power (Carrie's telekinesis, Ginger Snaps, The Witch's Thomasin) to menopause's cultural construction as loss and 'living decay'. Drawing on Mary Douglas and Kristeva on pollution and abjection, and on Deleuze and Guattari's 'becoming-woman' and bodies defined by capacities rather than fixed being, it argues that the female reproductive body is more often barren than fecund and that this state is another generative modality, not an absence. It reads the Western biomedical pathologisation of menopause (Wilson's Feminine Forever, HRT) as a Foucauldian disciplinary discourse, then tracks older women through Sunset Boulevard's Norma Desmond, the hagsploitation cycle (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Strait-Jacket, Hush Hush Sweet Charlotte), and The Taking of Deborah Logan, concluding that Jessica Lange's American Horror Story roles offer the fullest, sexually frank rebuttal to the abjection and invisibility of the ageing woman.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Art, Madness, and Syd Barrett
samples.relation: George Reisch reads The Wall through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: madness is not a brain lesion but a historical construction — Renaissance unreason, classical confinement, then Tuke's and Pinel's psychiatric regime in which the madman must know 'he is watched, judged, and condemned' until judgment is internalized — which explains why Pink imprisons himself brick by brick and asks at 'The Trial', 'Have I been guilty all this time?' The fascist worms and skinhead riots of 'Waiting for the Worms' are the same crusade for uniformity that drove Pink mad — Foucault's 'moral city' where 'virtue is an affair of the state' — so fascism and insanity are versions of each other, with Sartre's 'Hell is other people' from No Exit as the framing thought. Both the album ('Outside the Wall': 'the bleeding hearts and artists make their stand') and Foucault end by defending art as the last channel of unreason, and Reisch argues Syd Barrett's unanswerable absence was exactly that interrupting void powering 'Echoes', Dark Side, Wish You Were Here, and The Final Cut.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: The Male Vampire as Metrosexual . . . Sort Of
samples.relation: Joan Grassbaugh Forry asks how conventional standards of beauty, femininity, and masculinity operate in the vampire aesthetic of Interview with the Vampire, Buffy, and Queen of the Damned. Using Foucault's figure of the soldier whose body is 'made' by discipline, and Bartky and Bordo's feminist extension of it to dieting, deportment, and ornamenting the female body, she argues vampires expose the ideology of natural beauty: they are youthful, elegant, and effortlessly beautiful - no gym, no reflection - so their beauty is pure naturalness with the discipline erased. Gender decides the payoff: ultra-feminine female vampires (Drusilla's dresses and tea parties, Akasha, childlike Claudia) are femmes fatales whose threat must be punished by death, ridicule, or infantilization, while feminized male protagonists (Louis, Angel, Spike painting his nails and watching Passions - the 'metrosexual') win audience identification and tragic dignity. Beauty, in short, is a shield for the male vampire and a death sentence for the female.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Eckstrand uses Foucault to explain the show's central pattern that 'our thing is part of the big thing': power is exercised rather than possessed, flowing through networks in every direction, so even pawn Wallace can have kingpins, captains, and prosecutors running around after him, and McNulty's fake serial killer shows how the police-Sun-politics network can be worked from below. The stat game and standardized tests are Foucauldian power/knowledge, producing a truth ('shining up shit and calling it gold') that hides systemic crime and poverty while punishing truth-tellers like Daniels and reformers like Colvin and Freamon, and its three tools of discipline, hierarchical observation, normalizing judgment, and examination, are visible from Comstat and the project-class window to the grand jury that tames the dockworkers' union. Even reform becomes part of the machine it targets (Templeton's Pulitzer chase), so the best hope is the constant accumulation of small victories by those who keep fighting.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Make It So”
samples.relation: Challans argues Picard is 'Starfleet's conscience' because he exemplifies Kantian moral autonomy — acting on categorical principles like the Prime Directive rather than on orders, authority, or hypothetical imperatives — while the Borg show its total loss: assimilated drones forfeit moral agency, and the Borg Queen's pursuit of collective perfection is at best Rawls's merely 'rational autonomy.' Boétie's dupes and knaves, Nietzsche's herd, Milgram's obedience experiments, and Foucault's institutions producing docile bodies explain how war machines make complicity normal, from Gowron's corrupt Klingon Empire to Browning's 'ordinary men.' Picard passes the twenty-fourth-century Milgram tests — refusing illegal orders in 'Conundrum' and exposing 'The Pegasus', fighting Starfleet itself in Insurrection with 'How many people does it take, Admiral, before it becomes wrong?' — while the chapter closes by charging that America's real war machine now resembles the Borg more than Starfleet.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: Progress Is a Myth that Truly Makes Life Worthwhile
samples.relation: Garnar contrasts the material practice of collecting CDs -- shelving some 1,500-2,000 discs by genre, the Rachels' Egon Schiele packaging, and Humean associations binding particular discs to memories like buying blue hair dye the day he got New Order's Lowlife -- with the iPod-era 'iPhenomenon' of buying songs piecemeal from iTunes. Using William James's question 'How is the practice real?' he rejects the real/virtual split, and reads the freedom of iMedia as a corollary of Marx and Engels's 'single, unconscionable freedom -- Free Trade': the solipsistic consumer never confronts the artist the way the album as artifact (Coltrane's My Favorite Things ending, he realizes, had to end with 'But Not for Me') forces him to. The body supposedly made unnecessary by 'iLiving' remains, with Foucault, a site of discipline -- eating disorders, outsourced assembly labor, e-waste -- so he keeps his iPod but defends a plurality of media and calls progress a myth.

samples.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
samples.title: Beyond Panopticism The Biopolitical Labor of Surveillance and War in Contemporary Film
samples.relation: Gooch argues that the post-2005 surveillance film cycle moves 'beyond panopticism': Foucault's disciplinary gaze gives way to Deleuze's 'societies of control,' and the surveiling gaze becomes direct domination and a form of biopolitical labor (Hardt and Negri) rather than an impersonal structure. He reads the prestige dramas (Redacted, Stop-Loss, In the Valley of Elah, Lions for Lambs) as exposing the soldier's proletarianization and self-surveillance, and the thrillers/blockbusters (Déjà Vu, The Kingdom, Body of Lies, The Bourne Ultimatum, Eagle Eye, Burn after Reading) as staging a Marxist antagonism between living labor (the watching hero) and the fixed capital of surveillance technology. Using Deleuze's 'degraded time-image,' Kant's needed separation of subject and law, and Benjamin/Agamben's state of exception, he shows Eagle Eye inverting law and subject to justify preemptive war and turn biopolitical labor into the labor of subjection.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: Case the Promised Land
samples.relation: Herstein reads 'Thunder Road' as an event, not an object: the screen door slam and Mary's waving dress form a single event that language can only serially narrate, and Whitehead's event ontology (with Ricoeur's Time and Narrative on how we discover and rewrite ourselves in stories, and Emerson's 'monstrous corpse' of memory from 'Self Reliance') explains why the Seanachie's tale creates a world rather than describing one. samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jessica Miller shows Katniss coded masculine, since Collins built her from Theseus and Spartacus and her breadwinning, hunting, and defiance fit masculine norms, while Prim embodies everything Beauvoir says civilization 'produces' as feminine, and Panem itself proves oddly gender-neutral: women work the mines, Finnick is the sex symbol sold by Snow, and Coin is as ruthless as any man. samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man

samples.relation: Pye and O'Sullivan use Judith Butler's claim that gender is performative to read the walkers as genderless: they keep the trappings of biological sex but perform no gender, and like drag queens they 'trouble gender' when the little girl walker turns to face Rick. samples.book: 277 - Porn – Philosophy for Everyone - How to Think With Kink

samples.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
samples.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rood unpacks Klosterman's 'This Is Emo' thesis that no woman will ever satisfy him: women love Lloyd Dobler rather than John Cusack, and everyone measures real relationships against Hollywood fake love (Coldplay songs, the Woody Allen Personality Type) until, as Klosterman puts it, real people actively trying to live like fake people are no less fake. He reads this through Sartre's cafe waiter and Butler's gender performativity to argue identity is learned performance, and through Plato's cave updated to a reclining-seat movie theater where we mistake projected shadows for real love. samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abraham Schwab turns Ygritte's 'You know nothing, Jon Snow' into a theory of epistemic humility: Jon misreads wildling courtship norms, Sam's dragonglass shatters on wight Small Paul, Lord Mormont assumes Mance fights like a southern king and pays for it at the Fist of First Men, while Arya's accurate self-knowledge keeps her alive. samples.title: 48. The Matrix as Philosophy Understanding Knowledge, Belief, Choice, and Reality

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo

samples.relation: The Senors use Psych to separate true belief from knowledge: Shawn's hunch that Shabby the sea lion was murdered is true but shabbily evidenced, and his justified, true belief that a Clayton family member sabotaged the plane fails to be knowledge when the killer turns out to be a son-in-law he had no reason to think existed - a textbook Gettier case from 'He Dead.' samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter turns Raylan's claim that shooting Tommy Bucks was 'justified' into a question of epistemic justification, expounding Plato's Meno definition of knowledge as justified true belief, Gettier's 1963 counterexamples (rebuilt with Boyd truly but luckily predicting that a marshal will be arrested), and the repairs of Goldman's no-false-causal-link condition and Harman's inference to the best explanation. It then grades the show's reasoners: Raylan knows the Crowes rather than Boyd killed Wade Messer, Boyd knows Cassie milks the revival snakes' venom, Art Mullen does not yet know Raylan helped Winona return the evidence-room money, and gut-feeling victims like Ellen May do not know what they saw. samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 16. Getting at the Truth
samples.relation: The chapter sets out the Platonic justified-true-belief analysis of knowledge with Discworld examples—Archchancellor Ridcully as a fallible authority, the physics of thaum particles as coherentist justification—before constructing a Discworld Gettier case in which a young wizard sees a fake level-seven wizard killed and truly but accidentally reports that 'a level seven wizard was killed.' It then tests the standard repairs, applying Nozick's truth-tracking function and Goldman's causation function to a case where a man blames the notorious Reacher Gilt for a theft actually committed by the dwarf he bumped into, and argues that neither truth-tracking nor specificity makes the problem go away. The upshot is that Discworlders, used to expecting to be wrong, may let go of false 'knowledge' more easily than our confidently wrong Roundworld.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Using 'Flowers for Charlie', where a placebo pill convinces two scientists and even the Waitress that Charlie has become a genius, the chapter asks what actually makes something philosophy. Since we can never verify our premises or our reasoning, the chapter sides with Aristotle's response to Plato's theory of forms that we can never determine what a thing is, only what it is not, and concludes the show is philosophical precisely because the Gang is the exact antithesis of reality, truth, and right action.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: Education never ends Watson. It is a series of lessons with the greatest for
samples.relation: J. Solomon Johnson asks whether Holmes's conclusions are knowledge or luck, walking through justified true belief with a Holmesian Gettier case (Watson rightly believing the killer was a former ship hand for the wrong reason), Moore's proof that knowledge entails belief, and Russell's stopped clock as an unsafe belief. BBC Sherlock's fake Vermeer and the 2009 film's 'resurrected' Lord Blackwood illustrate beliefs that fail safety or sensitivity across nearby possible worlds, while 'The Stock-Broker's Clerk' shows Holmes's observation of the scorched slippers making his belief sensitive. samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Richard Greene asks what, if anything, walkers know. Walker behavior defeats Jenner's 'mindless instinct' line: Jenny turning the handle of her old house, the little girl walker retrieving her teddy bear, a walker smashing the department store window with a rock, and the horde seeing through Rick and Glenn's gut disguise once rain washes the scent away. samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Nys asks whether political correctness is a genuine moral demand or mere verbal hygiene, using the British Office: Gareth's racist BMC joke, Brent aborting it when Oliver the Black coworker arrives, the 'wanking claw' impression, and the porn email with Brent's head pasted onto a woman's body. He argues words genuinely wound (Brent's 'sticks and stones' rehearsal collapses when Gareth reveals his cruel nicknames) but that offense is wrong as disrespect for human equality rather than as a feeling, an account filled out with Frankfurt's claim that our identity depends on what we care about, so the non-targeted can be offended too. After weighing Mill's defense of free discussion for social progress, the pornography debate (in which reduction to body parts is exactly what degrades, as Brent complains he was 'objectified'), and Marx's notion of ideology as a concealing set of ideas behind a 'white male' bias, he concludes that Brent's flaw is looking good rather than being good, and that PC language is rhetorical make-up over persisting inequality.

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This composite chapter opens with the volume's Introduction and then runs several essays. Jeff McLaughlin's 'What If?' reads DC's Crisis on Infinite Earths and Marvel's What If? series as literal illustrations of Leibniz's possible-worlds metaphysics: the multiverse of Earth-1, Earth-2 and the 3,000 doomed universes dramatizes counterfactuals and Leibniz's Theodicy argument (via the principle of sufficient reason) that God actualizes only the best of infinitely many possible worlds, with Descartes invoked on why a perfect God permits imperfection. Amy Kiste Nyberg's essay analyzes the 1954 Senate hearings on EC horror comics (Gaines's 'The Orphan') as an applied-ethics clash between publishers' free expression and protecting children, explicitly deploying Mill's On Liberty and harm principle to argue why the child-audience framing defeats the anti-censorship case. samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Challenges the received libertarian message of 'Medicinal Fried Chicken' — Randy giving himself testicular cancer for a marijuana prescription, Cartman bootlegging KFC in a Scarface parody after Colorado bans fast food — by pressing Mill's liberty principle on what 'harm' means: Mr. Garrison's plot to murder the Queer Eye cast is immediate harm, but the S&M Mr. Slave displays to schoolchildren in 'The Death Camp of Tolerance' is only indirect, psychologically mediated harm Mill cannot clearly handle. Addiction then undermines Mill's assumption of sovereign tastes: corporations can shape desire without coercing anyone, so the libertarian 'omnicompetent individual' is a myth. Mead's intersubjectivity (Randy smoking pot before Officer Barbrady, blind to how Jimbo sees him) grounds the constructive claim that selves are socially formed, and the shark-tank defecation and Prisoner's Dilemma examples show why collective harms need rules and regulation.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: The Gathering of the Tribe Ironic Sacramentalism
samples.relation: Horace Fairlamb argues the Grateful Dead were the Sixties' real revolutionary success: where the New Left failed by keeping confrontational politics, the Dead changed consciousness first, extending Mill's liberal 'experiments in living' into a whole alternative culture. He reads the total improvisation learned at the Acid Tests ('the form that follows chaos'), the band's leaderless 'functional anarchy' — Lesh: if anyone tried to take charge 'it would just dissolve in their hands' — and its flat business hierarchy with roadies as corporate presidents as a spontaneous order lived at the edge of chaos. The Deadhead community's ritual communitas, analyzed through Victor Turner's separation-liminality-reincorporation model, amounts to an 'ironic sacramentalism' that achieves what social contract from Hobbes (force), Locke (property), and Rawls (self-interest) cannot: unity that transcends difference while leaving it in place.

samples.book: 101 - Discworld and Philosophy - Reality Is Not What It Seems
samples.title: 5. The Truth Shall Make Ye Fret
samples.relation: Watson uses The Truth - William de Worde's accidental invention of Ankh-Morpork's first newspaper and the plot to frame Lord Vetinari - to stage the three classic arguments for censorship: direct harm (character assassination 'works every day'), indirect harm (with MacKinnon's point that the speech of the dominant drowns out the subordinated, applied to speciesist insults at Koom Valley), and the false-beliefs argument. Against them stand the knowledge problem and the equality assumption: Mrs. Arcanum's deference to print, Vetinari's turtle-shaped-world joke, and the Montessori-Broca dispute show we never know in advance which beliefs are false, and any censor like Lord de Worde has his own agenda.
