samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Framed by Dickens's Jacob Marley, Walker asks whether Jobs deserved his posthumous accolades despite giving far less to charity than Bill Gates, and tests him under three frameworks. Aristotle's virtue ethics acquits him (character is judged holistically, and charity sits near the golden mean of open-handedness rather than being a checklisted duty); Mill's utilitarianism acquits him (his innovations maximized happiness and he violated no Harm Principle—though abandoning daughter Lisa counts as a harm); and Singer's drowning-child argument condemns him as near-morally-bankrupt for selling luxury gadgets while children starve. Kant both convicts (charity is an imperfect duty under the categorical imperative) and saves Jobs: treating the affluent individual as an end in himself, never merely a means to the destitute, blocks Singer's demand for giving to marginal utility.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: A Little bit of Messi for our Life
samples.relation: The authors cast the contrast between disciplined European and improvisational South American football as Mill's struggle between liberty and authority: the coach's tactical orders are 'rules of opinion' the genius may defy, as Maradona did on his sixty-meter run to the Goal of the Century, while the harm principle marks the line at the 'rules of law' — FIFA's Laws of the Game. The Hand of God goal, which broke even a rule of law yet stood because 'a goal is scored when the referee says so', illustrates Searle's point that football's regulative capacity cannot guarantee its agreements, leaving a gap filled only by ethics and fair play. Following Wittgenstein's 'ethics and aesthetics are one and the same', they conclude that a bit of Messi-style rule-breaking — Messi replicated both Maradona goals in 2007 — is what makes football, and life, joyful and beautiful.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Do We Attain Justice by Punishment
samples.relation: Kenny's blackmail arc in Shut Up and Dance — the twist that reclassifies the sympathetic protagonist as a child-pornography offender — anchors an argument that the hackers' vigilantism cannot attain justice: their punishments are unannounced, disproportionate, aimed at merely moral wrongs (infidelity, racist emails), and exempt from the presumption of innocence and nulla poena sine lege that states replaced vendetta with. A distinction between natural-law and legal-positivist conceptions of justice shows why punishment belongs to the state alone. Against retribution ('a mere prison sentence is too good for Kenny'), Bentham's and Mill's utilitarianism — deterrence, incapacitation, and above all rehabilitation, capped by the harm principle — shows punishment should be no more than deterrence requires, making the hackers sadists rather than agents of justice.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Added Time
samples.relation: McDermid takes Maradona's cheeky 'a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God' claim literally and asks what would make either 1986 goal against England—the obvious handball or the Goal of the Century—a miracle, using Aquinas's definition of miracles as intentional divine acts beyond the order commonly observed in nature. He explores how God could intervene without breaking natural law, analogizing God to a goalkeeper exempt from the handball rule or a spectator outside the game: in a deterministic world He could only arrange initial conditions (a domino setup requiring fine-tuning at the Big Bang), while in an indeterministic quantum world He could load the chancy micro-events along Maradona's mazy, sensitively balanced run. Hume's empiricist argument against miracles then shows we could never be justified in believing either goal miraculous, since the mundane explanation—Maradona's cheek and skill, lapses of concentration, a missed handball call—always has the whole of past experience on its side.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: The Epilogue A Question of Belief
samples.relation: Systematically pairs Hume's philosophy of religion with Python parodies: Anselm's ontological argument fails because existence cannot be defined into a concept (the Yeti-spotter who never spotted one), with Arthur 'Two Sheds' Jackson, Ron Obvious, and Confuse-A-Cat illustrating the gap between conceivability and possibility; the Galaxy Song's cosmic order and the mock hymn 'All Things Dull and Ugly' stage the design argument and Hume's reply that creation shows moral indifference as readily as benevolence; and Brian's 'miracles' — being 'taken up' then spotted sprinting, curing Simon the hermit by landing on his foot — illustrate Hume's 'Of Miracles' on the unreliability of testimony. Hume's Natural History claim that the cause of religion is fear surfaces in the 'O Father, please don't boil us' hymn and in Arthur's groveling before a God who hates it. Both Hume and the Pythons end in suspended judgment about God — settled, if at all, only by the wrestling match in which 'God exists by two falls to a submission.'

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Dueck takes Stan's closing pluralism in 'Super Best Friends'—all religions have something valuable to teach, as the interfaith superheroes' combined powers defeat Blaine—and tests it against Hick's pluralism, exclusivism, and Rahner's inclusivist 'anonymous Christians', using 'Go God Go's warring atheist factions to show exclusivity is unavoidable even without God. Hume's miracle argument explains why Jesus's look-away water-into-wine trick convinces no one in the episode: testimony can never outweigh the laws of nature, so supernatural evidence resists natural evaluation. Popper's falsificationism warns that watering doctrines down to make religions compatible (the rabbit-pope of 'Fantastic Easter Special') leaves nothing to test, while James's will to believe and Plantinga's defense of exclusivism ground the conclusion that faith can be rationally justifiable where evidence runs out—beware the Blainetologists, but do not surrender ways of life that define us.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a14.xhtml
samples.relation: Stewart argues Middle-earth magic is rule-bound engineering rather than Hume's miracle as 'a violation of the laws of nature': spells fail, the Ring hides neither shadow nor wet footprints, and magic comes in strengths like gravity, so fear of Gandalf is fear of superior knowledge of nature's laws, not of lawlessness. The deeper point is Tolkien's linkage of magic with technology as the impatient will to make one's will effective quickly - Sauron is 'Lord of magic and machines', the Ring is the supreme technological artifact, Saruman's forged men and blast-fires embody domination - while elvish 'Art' is sub-creation and Beorn's communion with animals models harmony with nature. Like Thoreau pricing possessions in 'how much life' they cost, the chapter ends with Tolkien's warning that 'if a thing can be done, it should be done' is the great false assumption of our age.

samples.book: 098 - The Princess Bride and Philosophy - Inconceivable!
samples.title: 1. True Love and False Fronts
samples.relation: Fallis argues the movie is really about lying and duplicity, not true love: Humperdinck frames Guilder for Buttercup's abduction, the Dread Pirate Roberts is a serial persona, and even the heroes bluff their way into the castle. He treats this as 'adversarial epistemology,' showing that Descartes's malicious demon and Kant's argument that universalized lying is impossible only rule out extreme scenarios and cannot unmask mundane deceivers like Vizzini and Humperdinck (a point he sharpens with Parfit's objection that liars sometimes profitably tell the truth). What does real work are Hume's tools for evaluating testimony: Valerie catches Miracle Max lying about 'to blave' by asking what he has to gain, and Buttercup catches Humperdinck when his claim that every ship in the armada will accompany the honeymoon contradicts his promise of the four fastest ships.

samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 11. The Truth about Lying
samples.relation: Fallis reads the series through the philosophy of testimony: TZ relentlessly punishes both truth-tellers (Bob Wilson's gremlin warning and nine more episodes) and liars ('Hocus-Pocus and Frisby,' 'The Four of Us Are Dying'), while Kant's letter on reticence suggests the untried third option of keeping quiet. On the receiving side, Hume's rules for discounting witnesses and his argument that one should never believe miracle reports explain why the crew disbelieves the gremlin and why 'Printer's Devil's' Devil reasons like Hume, Descartes' malicious demon returns in the disguised devils of 'The Hunt' and 'The Howling Man,' and the chapter ends endorsing Pascal's Wager: 'The Last Rites of Jeff Myrtlebank' argues we should believe even crazy, lying testimony just in case it is true.

samples.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
samples.title: GARDENING
samples.relation: O'Brien reads Voltaire's closing injunction in Candide, 'we must cultivate our garden,' through David Hume to argue that gardening is therapy—a retreat from metaphysics and religion into the tranquility of common life. Hume rejects belief in miracles and religious 'enthusiasm' not by logic but by recalling everyday reasoning (a melon seed, not a miracle, explains melons in the greenhouse), and the gardener is the sophisticated artisan-reasoner attuned to nature's regularities. Gardening inculcates Humean virtues (industry, patience, balancing action, pleasure and indolence) and Haybron's attunement/engagement/endorsement, yielding Epicurean ataraxia; the Sisyphean gardener (Camus) fighting slugs, and Wittgenstein taking up gardening as a cure, illustrate the point.

samples.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
samples.title: What of Philosophical Relevance Is there in Tarantino’s Films
samples.relation: Bruce Russell argues that Tarantino's films share a pattern—a cruel man's life goes awry, violence erupts, and glimpses of compassion appear, like Mr. White comforting the shot Mr. Orange—but that fiction can raise philosophical questions without justifying general philosophical theses. He uses the Pulp Fiction exchange over the bullets that missed Jules and Vincent to raise Hume's problem of miracles (divine intervention versus a 'freak occurrence'), and applies the accounts of Mill, Gibbard, Hare and Hume to show that even Vincent's twisted code—balcony drops for foot massages, execution for keying a car—counts as having a morality. His conclusion: the films raise, but never answer in depth, the questions of what a miracle is and what it is to have a morality.

samples.book: 018 - Harley-Davidson and Philosophy - Full-Throttle Aristotle
samples.title: Harley-Davidson and Philosophy
samples.relation: Responding to the Guggenheim's record-breaking 'The Art of the Motorcycle' show, Rollin argues that Dickie's institutional theory explains how motorcycles became art but not why people lined up, and offers three aesthetic lenses: Marinetti's Futurist celebration of machine speed, danger, and rebellion; Dewey's 'an experience', which every ride exemplifies, from his two-week trips with his son to the blown engine rescued by a ranch truck and the canned-spaghetti feast; and the Bauhaus doctrine that form follows function, making customized Harleys industrial sculpture that appreciates in value. He closes with Heidegger: riding's regular face-to-face with 'the possibility of the impossibility of one's being' is a call to authenticity and the final warrant for calling the motorcycle a fountain of aesthetic experience. American Indians revering Harleys as 'iron horses' illustrate the freedom and speed at the core of the bike's aesthetic pull.

samples.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
samples.title: 15. You Can’t Use My Name
samples.relation: Recounts how Hendrix changed law twice: ExperienceHendrix v. PPX (the 'You can't use my name' tapes) imported the Wrotham Park/Blake standard so breach-of-contract damages can reflect the infringer's gains rather than the victim's losses, and Experience Hendrix v. Hendrixlicensing.com used Washington's Personality Rights Act to extend postmortem publicity rights beyond the state of domicile, raising the constitutional problems Rossi identifies. The chapter then reads the dispute over whether the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' is art or noise through legal realism versus natural law theory and legal positivism — law as what courts actually enforce — and through the Institutional Theory of Art, with a Wittgensteinian cluster definition marking the essentialist route that failed.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: Something's Missing
samples.relation: Malloy tests three theories of art against Sabine Wren's graffiti and the Syndulla Kalikori: representation fails (her work is stylized beyond recognition and the collaborative Kalikori depicts nothing), expression fails (generations of makers make the Kalikori's expressive unity mysterious), and the institutional 'artworld' theory fails because Thrawn's curatorial authority destroys what it preserves — ripping a phoenix tag off its wall or displaying a still-growing Kalikori strips them of meaning. He concludes that defining art by any single feature (content, creation, or institutional context) is doomed, since Sabine's and Hera's works both are and are not art on every theory, and philosophy must keep searching for why they count as art.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 16. Can We All Get Along
samples.relation: Courtland Lewis tackles transitional justice after atrocity: with the Rising won, what is to be done with millions of Golds complicit in slavery, rape, and torture? He tests Peter French's virtuous vengeance—punishment that fits the wrong, grounded in Locke's natural rights—and finds Darrow's destruction of Gold society fails it (disproportionate, unsober, punishing young Julian for his ancestors' crimes), then turns to Jessica Wolfendale's argument that declaring anyone unforgivable adopts the wrongdoer's own devaluing outlook, exactly as Darrow becomes what he despises. The working model is South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission—confession, conditional amnesty, truth-telling, reparations, Tutu, Mandela, Beth Savage hoping to meet her bomber—applied to Mars through Mustang-style dignified engagement on Adam Michnik's model and Slavenka Drakulic's lesson that every Color inherits responsibility for rejecting the Society's past.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: John Irish reads the Amazon series' Vault 33 as Locke's Two Treatises staged and then betrayed: Overseer elections (Betty Pearson against Reg McPhee and Woody Thomas), town-council deliberation over captured Vault 32 raiders, and Lucy's 1950s-styled domesticity all mimic natural equality, consent of the governed, majority rule, and the preservation of property. Norm's discovery that every election is rigged in favor of cryo-preserved technocrats from Vault 31, that Lucy's marriage 'application' is engineered population control, and that Vault-Tec executives - including Lucy's mother Barb - voted to launch the Great War itself shows Locke's forms of consent, law, and rights preserved as empty ceremony. The chapter's argument is that Enlightenment liberalism stripped of transparency becomes authoritarian experiment management: consent becomes choreography in a commonwealth that is really a lab, right down to composting the raiders' bodies.

samples.book: 023 - James Bond and Philosophy - Questions Are Forever
samples.title: James Bond and Philosophy
samples.relation: Forster stages the dispute between Dr. No ('just a stupid policeman') and Scaramanga ('we are the same') over whether Bond's license to kill betrays the liberal rule of law it protects, connecting it to post-9/11 debates about executive power. He gives the rule of law a substantive ground in Locke's Two Treatises - prerogative power may suspend particular laws for the public good of preserving the community ('salus populi suprema lex'), illustrated by Locke's own career conspiring with Lord Ashley's spy network - and a procedural check in the separation of powers, mirrored in MI6's real parliamentary and judicial oversight. Both elements together, he concludes, let Bond's extra-legal work remain consistent with the rule of law: power exercised for the public good under institutional supervision, without which M's vendetta in 'For Your Eyes Only' would be indistinguishable from Scaramanga's contracts.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 12. Firefly as Philosophy Social Contracts, Political Dissent, and Virtuous Communities
samples.relation: Kowalski argues that Firefly and Serenity embody a distinctive political theory he calls 'Since I Found Serenity' (SIFS). The mindless, savage Reavers represent Hobbes's state of nature, showing government is necessary; but the Alliance's torture of River, the Miranda/Pax atrocity, and the murderous blue-gloved agents and Operative make a Hobbesian reading untenable and vindicate Locke's natural rights and right of revolution — Mal's 'I aim to misbehave' broadcast of the Miranda file is Lockean civil disobedience. He then presses the tacit-consent problem (the Browncoats cannot leave the 'Verse) and supplements Locke with Aristotle's friendship and community: Serenity's crew becomes a virtuous mobile commonwealth where friendship (Simon forgiving Jayne, Mal's 'love keeps her in the air') turns a commonwealth into a good-life community.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 6. Big Brother Ltd
samples.relation: Botello-Samson and Mobley extend Fromm's point that 1984 indicts authoritarian power in general by reading Oceania alongside neoliberalism, which grew out of Locke's liberalism of natural rights and limited government yet demands activist state power to create the conditions for markets. Doublethink reappears as 'accountable independence' in administrative law (Chevron deference, and Garcetti v. Ceballos stripping whistleblower protection) and as Washington Consensus food policy, in which developing nations were pushed off agricultural self-sufficiency while the US kept its own subsidies. Both Ingsoc and neoliberal governance reduce everything to economic elements and use Newspeak-like buzzwords such as 'stakeholder' and 'customer-driven government' to hide the contradiction between democratic rhetoric and rule by experts and elites.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Allen asks how a virtual war zone can exist inside the United States, starting from Hobbes: Marlo's cool killing of the security guard who just wants to be recognized as a man looks like the rights-free state of nature where 'nothing can be unjust.' But he argues Locke's sharper distinction fits better - the underclass are nominal citizens whose rights to life, policing, and education exist on paper while their substance is denied, which for Locke places an oppressed minority in a state of war within a state, and makes the drug game a rational choice for Michael, Dukie, and Randy. Marlo's 'you want it to be one way, but it's the other way' names that collapsed protection, and the chapter ends with Locke's warning that majority apathy lets oppression persist, reading The Wire as protest art meant to move viewers to political action.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 2 Transforming Wakanda Justice (or Not ) in Black Panther
samples.relation: Bein and Lewis imagine Killmonger surviving his duel to face Wakandan justice, and sort what justice would demand into retributive justice (Kant: punishment only what the offender deserves, never using him merely as a means to public safety, though they note Kant's own racist views), reparatory justice (Locke's natural rights and what Wakanda owes N'Jadaka for T'Chaka killing N'Jobu and abandoning him in Oakland), and the restorative-to-transformative justice of Changamire's gatherings in Coates's 'A Nation Under Our Feet,' modeled on South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission. They argue a restorative Wakanda would seat Killmonger with his victims and even the king at the table to repair harm rather than imprison him, and sketch a prison-abolitionist Wakanda meeting Thanos with 'Wakandan justice is more civilized.'

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 2. Sure We’re Criminals
samples.relation: Malloy asks whether the two law-breaking vigilantes are criminals and whether any duty to obey the law survives scrutiny. He runs consent theory through Superman surrendering in handcuffs in Man of Steel and the Red Son Superman's residence in the USSR, uses Darkseid's Apokolips as Hobbes's security sovereign against Locke's natural-rights limits, deploys Hume against tacit consent (Batman would never leave Gotham even in No Man's Land), and dismantles gratitude theory (the Kents' adoption involved a sacrificial choice the law cannot make) and fair play (Nozick's Batman-lottery undercuts "I'm not wearing hockey pads"). He lands near Wolff-style philosophical anarchism: Superman's constrained lawbreaking endorses the law's legitimacy while Batman treats law as one more tool in his war, making him a force of chaos.

samples.book: 014 - The Atkins Diet and Philosophy - Chewing the Fat with Kant and Nietzsche
samples.title: The Atkins Diet and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cox and Bender subject Atkins to Kant's universal-law formula — could every one of the billion overweight people on earth adopt it? — in a 'factive' thought experiment: a 25 percent rise in animal-protein output, nearly 250 million additional feed-grain acres, overgrazed ranges, and possibly a tenth of the world's remaining forests cleared for pasture. Calling Atkins reductionism's child (a metabolic switch judged on bathroom scales), they use Marx's 'metabolic rift' — soil nutrients shipped to cities, feedlots severing crops from livestock — and the Cartesian body-as-machine (via Federici) to place low-carb's atomized foods (bungalow subs, soy 'mashed potatoes,' pork rinds) as capitalism's latest rupture in the food system. Their verdict: only plant-leaning regimens could survive universalization, and the deeper fix is Wendell Berry's — eating understood as an agricultural act.

samples.book: 192 - Superman and Philosophy - What Would the Man of Steel Do_
samples.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
samples.relation: A scripted Lois Lane–Batman interview argues that the Batmobile/Batwing upgrade cycle and Wayne Enterprises' multinational production enact Marx's 'metabolic rift' (via John Bellamy Foster): both take from nature and return unprocessable waste faster than the planet can replenish, so protecting Gotham's way of life perpetuates an infinite environmental crisis of consumption. Solar-powered Superman wins the environmental showdown on lifestyle impact, but Batman counters that Krypton's ecological suicide makes Superman an 'environmental refugee,' not a model. The chapter's real verdict is Bruce's line 'We are all Bruce Wayne': human consumers must rebalance the human–nature relationship before finite resources like fresh water run out.

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 15. Infinite Environmental Crisis
samples.relation: Through a mock Lois Lane interview the chapter argues that Batman's endless Bat-vehicle upgrades and Wayne Enterprises' worldwide production repeat the 'metabolic rift' John Bellamy Foster developed from Marx: we take materials from the earth faster than we return them in a form it can process, generating an infinite chain of environmental crises. Superman looks like the winner because he runs on sunlight, yet Krypton died of its own ecological abuse, making him an 'environmental refugee' rather than a model. The real point is that 'we are all Bruce Wayne': humans cannot photosynthesize, so the choice is not Batman versus Superman but infinite consumption versus a balanced relationship with nature.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Luck as Anathema
samples.relation: Eylon and Horowitz defend the maligned manager's excuse 'we outplayed them and were plain unlucky' by distinguishing genuine football luck from fluke-luck: unlike sprinting, where outrunning your opponent and finishing fourth is incoherent, football's rules constitute rather than merely measure the skill, and 'almosts'—Roritania City hitting the woodwork eight times while United's one sloppy shot goes in—show ability and success genuinely coming apart. The accusation that football rewards the undeserving then exposes the control condition of moral desert, illustrated by two assassins whose shots differ only by an intervening swallow and by a never-bribed referee who would have taken the money, so that the luck football manifestly displays infects morality and politics generally. Football is anathema to some fans precisely because, unlike life where luck also rules, it displays luck inside an activity explicitly designed to reward merit—yet the authors conclude that 'almosts' and the all-or-nothing scoring are also the source of the game's beauty, and nobody who loves it would have luck removed.

samples.book: 100 - Batman, Superman, and Philosophy - Badass or Boyscout_
samples.title: 13. Time to Choose
samples.relation: Goldberg and Gavaler read the heroes' first-year comics (The Superman Chronicles, The Batman Chronicles) as rival moral codes: Superman is a "super consequentialist" out to benefit mankind - reforming the Blakely Mine owner, demolishing slums, buying back swindled stock - while Batman is a "dark deontologist" whose vengeance oath makes consequences irrelevant, waiting out the Joker's murders of Claridge, Wilde, and Judge Drake because catching the villain, not saving victims, is his duty. Mill's utilitarianism frames Superman's consequentialism and Kant's Groundwork - intentions over outcomes, the batarang blocked by invisible glass leaving Batman's morality untouched - frames Batman's, with moral luck the battleground: deontology shrugs it off, but Superman's powers let him smooth luck over too. On the opening dilemma, Superman defuses the bomb while Batman chases the villain, so the authors judge Superman's code superior because Batman's can let hundreds die without moral failure.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: George Dunn tests Katniss's luck-saturated life against Kant's claim that the good will shines 'like a jewel' regardless of fortune, with Peeta's vow to 'die as myself' as the stronghold the Gamemakers cannot touch, and with Seneca's dictum that what Fortune has not given she cannot take away. He then runs Nagel's four kinds of moral luck through the trilogy: Haymitch's reaping-made alcoholism as constitutive luck, Rue's death sparing Katniss an impossible final choice as circumstantial luck, Peeta's rooftop words echoing unconsciously behind the flowers for Rue as causal luck, and the revolution's success as resultant luck without which Katniss would have been the destroyer of District 12 rather than its torchbearer. Framing the Gamemakers as Fortuna on her wheel, he ends with the berries: since Katniss can never untangle whether she held them out from love, defiance, or self-protection, even moral worth proves hostage to luck and to the opacity of our own motives.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Michaud asks whether a prophesied savior can be a hero: since Lyra can succeed only in ignorance of the witches' prophecy (Dr. Lanselius's condition), either others keep her ignorant and she saves the world or someone tells her and she fails, so the outcome never depends on her any more than Iorek's eating of Iofur's heart depends on bear choice. Frankfurt's counterexample, recast with the Magisterium's Fra Pavel standing by to force your choice, shows one can be blameworthy despite being unable to do otherwise, and Fischer's guidance control, a reasons-responsive decision-making mechanism that is your own, checked across possible worlds, explains why responsibility survives absent alternatives. samples.title: 3 Sins of the Fathers Historical Injustice and Its Repair in lack Panther
samples.relation: Almassi contrasts Rawlsian ideal theory (the veil of ignorance, justice as fairness) with Charles Mills's critique that idealization marginalizes actual historic oppression, arguing the film's characters seek Aristotle's corrective justice in a world already steeped in wrongdoing: the 1991 deaths of W'Kabi's parents at Klaue's hands and of N'Jobu at T'Chaka's. He works through the Museum of Great Britain axe scene as restitution, W'Kabi's 'you kill him where he stands' and Killmonger's 'I'mma make sure we're even' as retribution (tested against Walen's proportionality principles, with vengeance untethered from legitimate punishment), and Nakia's and T'Challa's outreach centers as Margaret Urban Walker-style relational repair, reading T'Chaka's concealment of N'Jobu's death as actively constructed ignorance in service of isolationism.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 14. The Doctor as Philosopher The Collectivist-Realist Pacifism of the Doctor and the Quest for Social Justice
samples.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a 'collectivist-realist pacifist': morally opposed to war yet willing, as a last resort, to use lethal force for social justice. She places the Doctor on Cady's warism-to-pacifism continuum (past absolute and collectivist pacifism), augmenting it with Martin Luther King Jr.'s realist pacifism — ethical appeals 'undergirded by constructive coercive power' — and Gandhi's ahimsa and belief that no one is beyond redemption (the Doctor sparing Davros, offering enemies a choice). She tests Kant's duty ethics and respect for persons (Rule 1: the Doctor lies), Ross's prima facie duties, Mill's utilitarianism ('The Fires of Pompeii,' 'The Beast Below'), Gilligan/Noddings care ethics, and Wolterstorff's 'life of needs,' and reads 'The Day of the Doctor' as a Rawlsian veil of ignorance brokering Zygon-human peace.

samples.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
samples.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
samples.relation: Stephen Kershnar examines the three strongest arguments for the IOC's ban on performance-enhancing drugs, harm-to-self, harm-to-others, and unfairness, and argues each fails, using cases such as Ben Johnson's stripped 1988 gold and Marion Jones. Against harm-to-self he cites anti-paternalism and the far greater accepted risks of NFL play and boxing; against harm-to-others he shows PED pressure is no different from the pressure of rivals' superior training (a Prisoner's Dilemma leagues need not solve); against unfairness he tests four accounts of fairness, including a Rawlsian veil-of-ignorance model whose choosers might find banning steroids while allowing Lasik and high-tech gear arbitrary. He concludes the ban, if justified at all, rests only on contested utilitarian grounds like audience preference and protecting children.

samples.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
samples.title: Reality versus Revolution
samples.relation: McPherson argues political rap has never been politically revolutionary, sorting it into three schools: the amoral "gangsta Hobbes" ethic (Mobb Deep's "Survival of the Fittest", 50 Cent's "get rich or die tryin'") that sees the hood as Hobbes's state of nature where no social contract with blacks ever existed; Afrocentric communitarianism, split between nationalist separatists (Brand Nubian, X-Clan, Dead Prez) and the more cosmopolitan Native Tongues (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest); and a radical liberalism closer to Rawls than its adherents admit. Against Chuck D's "What's a smilin' face when the whole state's racist?", he argues Rawls's original position, veil of ignorance, and difference principle - applied with real-world knowledge of racism - support rather than oppose Public Enemy's demands for racial justice.
